hook.text: In 1994, Britain privatized its railways, splitting track from train operations.

buildup.text: The theory: competition would cut costs and improve service. Reality was messier.

discovery.text: Multiple firms ran trains on shared tracks. Coordination was chaotic for passengers.

twist.text: Japan privatized railways in 1987 and it worked brilliantly. The difference was execution.

climax.text: Britain is now re-nationalizing its railways, reversing decades of private control.

punchline.text: Privatization works when rail stays a system, not parts.

quiz.question: Why did Japan's rail privatization succeed while Britain's struggled?
